parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no border or document friction, no state hostility; national self-ID law, and a hate-crime aggravation documented as applied in practice (Vigo 2026 fine; Valencia gang case producing a prison sentence) — working, if limited, recourse. Documented social acceptance is strong but its measures are dated (2013/2016 polls predating the 2023 law); current signals are official/tourism framing and favourable foreign travel advice. Negatives: one region (the capital) repealed its non-discrimination law and trans-relevant conversion-therapy penalties and recognitions — largely resident-facing, but it removes local recourse and signals uneven climate; conservative attitudes outside big cities; violence trend data conflicting and not trans-specific. The precise legal basis for facility access is unresolved (open question, not a documented exposure). Net: solid acceptance-plus-working-protection tier, held a step below the strongest anchors by uneven regional protection and thin current attitudinal data.
